canonical_title: Recovery from post-stall gyrations and spins

versions.title_at_revision: Recovery from post-stall gyrations and spins
versions.text: Criterion: Verify that recovery from post-stall gyrations and spins is safe. Standard: The air vehicle meets the standards within the following MIL-STD-1797 paragraphs: a. 5.2.5.6 Recovery from post-stall gyrations and spins. b. 5.2.5.6.1 Turns and altitude loss for recovery (see table LXXXVI for guidance). c. 5.2.5.6.2 Avoidance of spin reversal. d. 5.2.5.6.3 Control forces for recovery (see table LXXXVII for guidance). e. 5.2.5.6.4 Operation of automatic stall, departure, spin prevention or recovery devices. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, simulation, and inspection of process, requirements, design, test, and configuration documentation. Additional Reference: 14 CFR 23.203 Turning flight and accelerated turning stalls; 23.221 Spinning

versions.title_at_revision: Recovery from post-stall gyrations and spins
versions.text:
Standard: The proper recovery techniques are easily apparent to the pilot, are simple and easy to apply under the motions encountered, and provide prompt recovery from all post-stall gyrations, incipient spins, and developed spins. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis and simulation to assess recovery the techniques for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess the recovery techniques for each combination of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess the recovery techniques for selected combinations of regions of handling qualities, air vehicle states, flight phases, and environmental conditions.
